label: paragraph_title
text: "SPLASHED WITH BLOOD." FULL STORY OF WANHSIEN EPIC.

label: text
text: DEAD SOLDIERS HEAPED UP IN PYRAMIDS.

label: text
text: Details of the Wanhsien incident make a story that is certainly unique in the annals of the Yangtze. Indeed it is unlikely that a bloodier fight has ever been fought in China waters. The whole scene as the survivors paint it does not belong in this age but in the 18th century, when muzzle to muzzle fighting was the rule.

label: text
text: The "Kiawo" was fitted with boiler plate, equipped with two pom-poms, fore and aft, and a number of machine and Lewis guns.

label: text
text: It was planned that four boarding parties should enter the four after cargo doors in the starboard quarter of the s.s. "Wanhsen," get on deck and stand off the soldiers until the three officers had made their escape.

label: text
text: The first man who stepped across into the cargo door was greeted with a riffle bullet. The second was also shot at and then

label: paragraph_title
text: YANG SEN'S REPRISALS

label: paragraph_title
text: Takes Three British Missionary Captives.

label: text
text: The bugle sounded and the four boarding parties leaped across and were met with a terrific crisscross machine gun fire that seemed to come from every part of the steamer.

label: text
text:
Machine guns had been placed to fire from every possible angle while riffemen by the score were concealed behind heaps of cargo.
The fight began at 6.28 p.m. and lasted for just three quarters of an hour with the two boats bound together by the "Kiawo's" grappling hooks.

label: text
text: Shanghai Sept. 17.

label: text
text: In the first few minutes the British sailors suffered all the casualties, but swarms of soldiers then appeared on the decks and the machine and Lewis guns came into full play.

label: text
text: The Wanhien's military have occupied the China's Inland Mission there and are holding three British missionaries as captives. --Reuter.

label: text
text: The “Kiawo” edged up, until she was fully abeam of the “Wanhsien” and the after pom-pom got into action against the after deck of the “Wanhsien,” with the shells set so that they would ex-plode four or five feet from the muzzle.

label: text
text: The dead on the deck of the "Wanhsien" heaped up until they rolled off the pile and fell into the water.

label: text
text: Hankow, Sept. 10.

label: text
text:
Muck of Brains and Filth.
On the forward hatch, which is a very big one, they piled up in a perfect pyramid as the "soldiers were driven on deck by the boarding parties below and mounted on the heap of corpses to get a shot at the "Kiawo" only to add to the heap. The whole port side of the "Kiawo" was splashed with blood until she appeared to have been newly painted with red lead and the deck of the "Wanhsien" was deep in a muck of blood, brains and filth.

label: text
text: The forward boarding party under a warrant officer got from the lower to the main deck and tried to find the ship's officers who were supposed to be locked in their cabins. It was discovered then that they were on the bridge, where they had fortified themselves against the pirates who had seized the ship.

label: text
text:
How Darley Was Killed, Commander Darley was on the bridge with several men who were sniping at soldiers on the "Kiawo" while the Chinese pilot fed them ammunition. Having gone so far, and having seen so many of his men killed and wounded, he must have made up his mind to take the "Wanhsen" while he was about it, for he ran down to the main deck with a revolver in each hand, shouted to his men who rushed to follow him and leaped across. Before he reached the body of the "Wanhsen" he fired two shots and then dropped fairly, riddled by machine gun fire. The Chinese immediately rushed him, stabbed him everywhere with their bayonets and cut his throat.
When about 300 out of the 400 soldiers on the "Wanhsen" had been killed, the rest grew frenzied in their desperation and made, a rush to board the "Kiawo."

label: text
text:
They were beaten back with the greatest difficulty and at the expenditure of the last cartridge on the "Kiawo," so the officers hastened to cut adrift and pull away.
As the ship fell away, the Chinese soldiers rushed forward on the "Wanhsen," got under the forecastle head where they had machine guns placed and opened a galling fire. The forward pompom placed a few shells neatly under the forecastle head and blew it off.

label: text
text: While all this was going on, the "Cockchafer" down stream and the "Widgeon" up stream were being vigorously shelled by the shore batteries on both sides of the river and were busy silencing them.

label: text
text: When the "Kiawo" was going from the "Wanhsien" to the "Wantung" a gun on the foreshore, just below the town of Wanhsien, opened on her.

label: text
text: The first shot fell about 20 yards ahead of her, but the second carried away her water tank and other gear above decks," so the "Cockchafer" let the shore gun have a six-inch shell and when the dust and smoke cleared away there were neither gun nor men to be seen, but only a great hole in the beach.

label: text
text: The “Widgeon” devoted herself chiefly to blowing up artillery and soldiers on the waterfront; but the “Cockchafer” with her bigger guns shelled the town.

label: text
text: Some say 39 shots were fired, others say 56, but not many had dropped into the town before it was burning from end to end and before it was all over the place was a raging inferno.

label: text
text: The "Kiawo" saw the last of this hideous picture at 8 p.m. when she dropped five miles down stream to anchor for the night. Even there they could see the red in the sky all night long. No one ate and no one slept that night, and some of the men are shaking yet from the excitement. —Rodney Gilbert to the "N. C. Daily News."

label: paragraph_title
text: 5.000 CASUALTIES?

label: paragraph_title
text: British Wounded Walk Down Gangway.

label: paragraph_title
text: Hankow. Sent. 10

label: text
text: Of the wounded on board the "Kiawo" taken over by the U.S. destroyer "Stewart", near Hanknow, there have been no deaths among the 14 and one man only is in a dangerous condition. Four were described as stretcher cases but all but the one man, who is shot through the kidneys, walked down the gangway.

label: text
text: All the dead, seven altogether, and the fourteen wounded, were carried away by the repulsed boarding party except Commander Darley whose body could not be recovered.

label: text
text: When the party returned decimated there was nothing to do but demonstrate to Yang Sen and his cut-throats that the threat to shell Wanhsen was not a bluff, so it was done and done thoroughly. According to an American report from Szechuan those killed in the bombardment numbered 5,000. The Japanese minimum estimate is 5,000.

label: text
text: Unfortunately for the “face” of the expedition and the security of foreign residents in Szechuan it was then found that none of the ships had more than enough fuel to take her back to Ichang so an immediate withdrawal from the scene was essential although it was fully realised

text: (Continued on Page 7.)

label: paragraph_title
text: ANTI-BRITISH.

label: text
text: AGITATION BEGINS IN HANKOW.

label: text
text: Important despatches on the developments at Hankow and further up the Yangtze River have been sent by Mr. Rodney Gilbert.

label: text
text: The position of the British Navy following the Wanhaien incident, the result of firing by the southerners and agitation for an anti-British boycott, and other incidents are described, throwing considerable light on the situation.

label: text
text: The latest despatch to hand ends:—

label: text
text: garrison troops under command of Gen. Tu Hsi-chun were yesterday disarmed and deprived of their uniforms by the southern troops. Without any previous arrangement they marched up the British Bund last night and boarded two Japanese steamers, the "Fengyang-Maru" and the "Suiyang Maru," hoping to be taken to Nanking whence they

label: text
text:
The situation was delicate because they amounted to over 2,000 men while the Japanese steamers were able to take only 500 and the balance refused to return into Chinese territory.
This predicament has now been relieved by other shipping companies who will take on board over 1,500 men to night.

label: text
text: As the result, of personal interviews between the American Consul, the Japanese Admiral Nagano and Gen. Tang Sui were "living on steamers here has been stopped. The American gunboat "Palos" and "Pigeon" with two steamers in convoy last night received a formal call from the officer commanding the batteries at Yochow who had boasted that he would allow no gunboat to pass Chenlingchi.

label: text
text: The British monitor H.M.S. "Cri-ket" took up her station to-dry at Chenlingchi without any incident.

label: text
text: Official telegrams from Chung-king give positive assurance that there is overt hostility against foreigners there, but nevertheless agitators are frantically working up a British boycott.

label: paragraph_title
text: Cameron Waiting?

label: text
text: Wachang is still resisting and though it is pretending to welcome peace overtures, is actually playing for time still hoping for Marshal Wu Pei-fu's return.

label: text
text: The local press adopts the Kuomintang tone, launching absurd charges of British support being given to Marshal Wu Pei-fu. They are also giving grossly distorted versions of the Wanhsen incident. Rumours of Gen. Yang Sen's affiliation with the Cantonese are given colour to by references to his army, in Kuomintang versions of the Wanhsen incident, as "our troops."—"N.C. Daily News."

label: paragraph_title
text: FOREIGNERS EVACUATE.

label: text
text: Reports from Ichang state that the Wanhsien British members of the Customs and Chinese Post Office staff have arrived at Ichang safely.

label: text
text:
One Customs' officer named Davies, who had been imprisoned, narrowly escaped being shot. He was finally released only as a result of the energetic action of the Japanese Commissioner of Customs.
—Reuter.

label: paragraph_title
text: JAPANESE PRISONERS.

label: paragraph_title
text: Shanghai, Sept. 17.

label: text
text: A message from Hankow under yesterday's date snys that the Japanese staff of the Talan Cotton Mill, Chiakow, have been made prisoners in the mill buildings by local labour union pickets. It is thought that this is a sequel to the present anti-Japanese agitation.

label: paragraph_title
text: WUCHANG ON FIRE.

label: paragraph_title
text: SOUTHERNERS CONTINUE ATTACK.

label: paragraph_title
text: Hostilities Start in Kiangsi

label: text
text: NATIONALISTS ADVANCE SLOWLY: A NEW ALLIANCE?

label: text
text: Hostilities between the southerners and their rivals continue but fighting must have been on a small scale. Holding the balance of power, Marshal Sun Chuan-fang is still retiring his men from war zone. Chinese men-of-war have been asked to join in and Wu Pei-fu is still moving his "crack" troops up, hoping to rescue Wuchang.

label: text
text: [By Our Special Correspondent.]

label: text
text: Later reports confirm the bombardment of Wuchang by the southerners lasting from Monday night till Tuesday afternoon.

label: text
text: Artillery was brought up to several positions and aeroplanes dropped bombs.

label: text
text: Fire broke out in "several places in the city.

label: text
text: The last message is that the northerners are still in possession. General Liu Yu-chen favours holding out but his colleague, General Chen Chia-mo prefers to make terms, which include 7 months' arrears of pay and safe conduct to Ichang.

label: text
text: In Kiangsi, the Nationalists are advancing slowly. Their two lines, in the north and south of the province, respectively, both met the garrisons of the "Five Provinces," who retired.

label: text
text: Marshal Sun Chuan-fang is now devoting attention towards an alliance with Fengtién, to ensure peace in the north-east, so that he can take the field against the southerners. His generals are moving towards the bigger towns on the Kiangsi frontier.

label: paragraph_title
text: Warships Join Flight?

label: text
text: A Nationalist report claims uninterrupted march en route to Nanchang, capital of Kiangsi.

label: text
text: On Sun Chuan-fang's side, his gunboats and one detachment has joined hands with northerners from Hankow the concentration being at Wuyueh.

label: text
text: The Nationalist 7th Army, fresh from its laurels in the Wu-Han sector, is moving against Wuyueh. To reinforce his strength there, Sun Chuan-fang has summoned Admiral Yang, Shu-chuang from Foo-chow to Shanghai, with a view to sending the warships in Fukien to the Yangtse.

label: text
text: Of these ships, Tuchun · Chow, Yam-yun is stated to have retained the "Hai" Yung" (recently a visitor

text: PIECE OF FOLLY:

label: paragraph_title
text: CHINA'S ELECTION TO COUNCIL

label: text
text: STRAIGHT TALKING.

label: text
text: Some criticism is made by the newspapers of the election of China and the South American States to the Council of the League of Nations, especially in view of China's lack of an effective Government.

label: text
text:
The Daily Express characterisises the election of China as a gigantic piece of folly.
Reuter.

label: paragraph_title
text: SALES ROOM CLAIM.

label: paragraph_title
text: SUING THE WRONG PERSON?

label: text
text: $173,20 FOR GOODS.

label: text
text: In the weekly Summary Court case fixing this morning a claim for $173,20 by Mr. W. J. Rowe against Mr. L. E. S. Hodge was mentioned.

label: text
text: Plaintiff appeared in person, defendant being represented by Mr. Hugh-Jones.

label: text
text: Plaintiff stated that the claim was for the price of certain goods and articles of furniture, realised at a sale at Mr. Hodge's sales rooms.

label: text
text: Mr. Hugh-Jones said that perhaps he ought to tell the plaintiff that he was suing the wrong person. He should have sued the Auctioneering and Brokering Company.

label: text
text: Plaintiff replied that he had dealt with Mr. Hodge as an auctioneer direct and not with the Company.

label: text
text:
His Honour adjourned the case for a week.
Three other Northern cruisers, at present in "Shantung waters," are under orders to leave for Hankow to assist Wu Pei-fu. They are the "Hai Sum," "Cho Yu" and "Yung Cheung," which were in Canton a few years ago on the southerner side. But are now under General Chang Tsung-chang, the Fengtien, tupan of Shantung.

label: text
text: General Chang Tsung-chang also intends to send an air force to the northerners, and to allot them more trains on the Peking-Hankow rail-way.

label: text
text: Wu Pei-fu's crack divisions, having arrived at the new base in Sinyang, have moved up to the 2nd line at Kwangshui and the 1st line at Hsianokun.

label: text
text: Only small numbers of southerners have left Hankow, northwards along the railway to attack Wu Pei-fu. The remainder are at Wuchang, further south in Hunan province, or moving towards Kingesi in two routes.

label: paragraph_title
text: Arsenal Busy

label: text
text: Prominent officers of "the" northern government state that General Cheng Kai-shek, after capturing the Frankow arsenal, will use that as a base.

label: text
text: They say he will immediately commence a march on Shanghai, defended by Marshal Sun Chuan-Tung. Overland, Hankow is more than 400 miles from Shanghai, much further by the river.

label: text
text: Marshall Sun, though suspected of being secretly in league with the southern general, is openly making every effort to defend Shanghai. The Shanghai arsenal is working night and day and the long range cannon at the Woosung forts have been repaired and put into first class condition.

label: paragraph_title
text: Cruisers At Shanghai.

label: text
text: Three of the best cruisers in the Chinese fleet, are at the mouth of the Yangtze. Recruiting is conducted at feverish pace in the country and village districts of Klangsu province, while the War Council have a complete list of stemmers and schedules, ready for the transport of troops upriver to meet the advancing Cantonese. — United Press.

label: text
text:
General Wu Pei-fu is organising his forces at Sianan, 80 miles north of Hankow, and is receiving representatives of Marshal Sun Chuan-fang with the object of co-operation. Marshal Chang Tso-lin will preside at a general military conference at Peking soon to be held.
"Associated Press."

label: paragraph_title
text: OLD LADY RESIDENT'S DEATH.

label: text
text: MRS. G. P. LAMMERT.

label: text
text: As we go to press we learn of the sad news of the death of Mrs. Geo. P. Lammert, wife of Mr. G. P. Lammert, Sr., the stockbroker.

label: text
text: Mrs. Lammert has for some time past been suffering from anaemia.

label: text
text: Yesterday, we are told, she was very cheerful and did not seem to be near such a serious turn that took place this morning.

label: text
text: The deceased lady died at 1.30 p.m. to-day.

label: text
text: Arrangements for the funeral will be announced later.

label: text
text: The sympathy of all will go out to Mr. Lammert and his family, and to other relatives, in this sad hour of their bereavement.
